item.text: I’ll check official tokenizer guidance for OpenAI and Anthropic, and distinguish a general rule of thumb from an exact per-text comparison—token counts vary with the actual wording.

There isn’t a fixed number of extra tokens: it depends on the exact text and tokenizer. OpenAI and Claude use different tokenizers, and neither provider publishes a single Korean-to-English conversion rate.

A rough planning estimate is **about 1.5–2× as many tokens for Korean as for an English translation**—so 1,000 English tokens might correspond to roughly **500–1,000 more tokens** in Korean. Treat that as an estimate, not a guaranteed ratio; the translations may also differ in length and wording.

For a precise comparison, count the *same meaning expressed in matched Korean and English text* using each provider’s tokenizer. OpenAI provides a tokenizer tool and notes that non-English text can use more tokens per character; Anthropic provides a token-counting API for Claude.

Sources: [OpenAI tokenizer](https://platform.openai.com/tokenizer) · [OpenAI: What are tokens and how to count them](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/4936856-what-are-tokens-and-how-to-count-them) · [Anthropic: Token counting](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/token-counting)
